chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Prayer is performed over the funeral at any hour, for it is not a prayer of bowing and prostration; rather, prayer is disliked at the rising of the sun and at its setting, which is when there is bowing and prostration, because it sets between the horns of Satan and rises between the horns of Satan.
Al-Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And there is no objection to praying over the deceased without ablution, and likewise for the one in a state of major ritual impurity (junub).

key_terms.بَيْنَ قَرْنَيْ شَيْطَانٍ: Between the horns of Satan (idiom for disliked times)
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الرُّكُوعِ وَالسُّجُودِ: Prayer of bowing and prostration (referring to regular Salat)
key_terms.لِلْجُنُبِ: For the one in major impurity

ai.seo_question: Is ablution required for funeral prayer and can it be performed at any time?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that Salat al-Janazah is exempt from the specific times of makruh (disliked) prayer—sunrise and sunset—because it lacks the full ritual prostration (sujood) associated with those periods. Shaykh al-Tusi adds the jurisprudential nuance that since wudu is not required, the state of major impurity (junub) does not hinder the performance of the funeral prayer, emphasizing its flexibility as a communal obligation.
